description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Opengrep SARIF fixture whose uriBaseId chain is well-formed, acyclic, short and syntactically valid and yet terminates on a relative reference, so no absolute ancestor exists to anchor it. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/ -- resolve_uri_base and resolve_sarif_location in paths.py, the classification order in adapters/sarif.py, FIELDS in emit.py and count_records in reconcile.py -- and only then cross-checked against the modules; none was taken from a run and transcribed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. Key names follow expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json, the template this folder's negative expected files share, so one generic loader reads all of them; the blocks this condition needs and that one does not -- terminal_case, four_deliberate_negatives, distinguished_from, conditionality, expectation_form, root_precondition, branches, cross_branch_invariants and how_a_test_drives_both_branches -- are additive and sit outside rows, row_derivations, rejections, counts and counters, which a loader reads unchanged.

fixture.derivation: A negative fixture is derived from the captured one rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated as a derivation. One result is unmodified captured output: /runs/0/results/0 is deep-equal to harness/artifacts/raw/opengrep.sarif results[432] and to the positive fixture's results[1] -- uriBaseId '%SRCROOT%' included, since the engine stamps it on every result. /runs/0/results/2, the defective record, is that artifact's results[0] (the positive fixture's results[0]) with exactly one field changed: its artifactLocation.uriBaseId from '%SRCROOT%' to 'SRCROOT'. /runs/0/results/1 is synthesized. The run also gained an originalUriBaseIds object, which the captured artifact does not emit at all.

one_field_derivation.everything_else_is_byte_identical: Verified by deep-equality: substituting '%SRCROOT%' back into the fixture's results[2] reproduces harness/artifacts/raw/opengrep.sarif results[0] exactly, and the positive fixture's results[0] exactly. The record's ruleId, message, fingerprints, properties, region and snippet are captured output.
one_field_derivation.why_one_field: A record defective in two ways would not tell a reader which guard rejected it. The two base identifiers differ by their percent delimiters alone, so the record is well-formed in every respect except which of the two chains it points at -- and the two chains are the whole content of this fixture.

fixture.captured_provenance: The synthesized record /runs/0/results/1 appears in neither harness/artifacts/raw/opengrep.sarif nor oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/opengrep.sarif: searched by uri substring across all 1322 captured results, which carry no finding for OneForOneBlockPusher.java at all. It borrows the ruleId and message of the hardcoded-conditional rule and names a real location -- its region.snippet matches lines 131 to 137 of that file in the pinned tree byte for byte. It is the same synthesized record the dangling-base sibling carries as its defective record, here pointed at the resolving chain instead, which is why it is a contrast row in this fixture and a rejection in that one.

snippets_verified_against_the_pin.method: Each region.snippet.text was compared byte for byte with the corresponding line span of the file in $SPARK_SRC. All three match.

fixture.rules_are_captured_verbatim: Both rule objects are deep-equal to their captured originals -- harness/artifacts/raw/opengrep.sarif tool.driver.rules[529] and rules[1458] respectively -- so every severity literal and every tag this file reports is the ruleset's own, not an authored one. The fixture carries two rules rather than 2002 because only two are referenced.
fixture.not_records: The run carries four members -- invocations, originalUriBaseIds, results and tool. Two of them are finding-shaped to a careless reader and are not records. The invocations[0].toolExecutionNotifications array holds two entries, both verbatim from the captured artifact's 51 (its first two, with executionSuccessful true): they are a Timeout and a Syntax error notification about a vendored d3.min.js, which is tool telemetry rather than a finding, and neither reconcile.count_records nor the adapter reads them. The four originalUriBaseIds entries are base declarations, not records. Counting either would move the raw side of the reconciliation identity and break it against an adapter that counts neither.
fixture.recorded_digest_is_the_tripwire: The sha256 and byte count above are re-derived when the fixture changes, never adjusted to keep a test green. A fixture edited to make an assertion pass is a fixture that no longer captures anything.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape.is_sarif -- a version of "2.1.0" together with a runs array; those two together are the whole test
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route("opengrep", doc) returns tool "opengrep", shape "sarif", adapter "sarif", scanner_class "sast"
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No normalize.shape.UnknownArtifactShape is expected here. The enclosing document is valid SARIF 2.1.0 -- a base map whose outermost entry is relative is not a malformed envelope -- and it routes cleanly; exactly one record inside it is defective, and the adapter rejects that record while still emitting the others. The fixtures that own shape-detection failure are near-sarif-version-only.json, near-sarif-runs-only.json and unknown-shape.json.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py and does not use this fixture.

terminal_case.this_fixture_covers: a uriBaseId chain that terminates on a relative reference with no absolute ancestor. AAP 0.5.4 names it as the third of the three terminal cases and, unlike the first, does not route it through the documented degenerate-base fallback: it is a rejection.
terminal_case.walk_outcome_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the BASE_OUTCOME_NO_ABSOLUTE_ANCESTOR constant -- a literal member of paths.BASE_OUTCOMES, the closed set of seven. Asserted against the module rather than by eye.
terminal_case.walk_detail: the chain SRCROOT -> PROJECTROOT ends on the relative reference 'project/' with no uriBaseId to resolve it against, so no absolute ancestor exists
terminal_case.mechanism: resolve_uri_base accumulates each relative level and joins it beneath the first absolute ancestor it finds. SRCROOT's uri 'src/' is relative, so it is pushed onto the suffix list and the walk moves to its parent PROJECTROOT. PROJECTROOT's uri 'project/' is also relative and it carries no uriBaseId of its own, so there is no parent left to move to and no absolute value to join the accumulated suffixes beneath. The walk returns rather than inventing an anchor.
terminal_case.why_this_is_the_easiest_of_the_five_to_o: Every other terminal case announces itself: a dangling identifier is a failed lookup, a cycle repeats, an over-deep chain counts past a bound, an invalid URI will not parse. This chain looks healthy at every step -- present identifiers, distinct, short, all URIs valid -- and fails only an absoluteness check a resolver must make deliberately. A consumer that joins the accumulated relative levels together and returns 'project/src' would produce a plausible base, resolve every record beneath it, and emit rows whose paths are wrong in a way nothing in the artifact contradicts.
terminal_case.plausible_producer_mistake: It mirrors SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.14.14's own chaining structure -- an originalUriBaseIds entry expressed relative to another -- with the single difference that the outermost base is relative rather than absolute. Research corroborates the neighbourhood rather than this exact string: AAP 0.2.2 records a producer emitting a degenerate ROOTPATH of file:/// inside a git repository (trivy issue 10364) and another emitting a uriBaseId with no matching originalUriBaseIds entry at all (semgrep issue 10591). Both are the same class of defect -- a base map that does not name a usable root -- which is why this case is a fixture whether or not this run's own artifacts contain it.
terminal_case.completes_the_set: With reject-sarif-uribaseid-missing-base, -cycle, -overdepth and -invalid-uri, this is the fifth and last of the uriBaseId fixtures, and the set now covers every terminal case AAP 0.5.4 names rather than collapses: absent, cycle, over-depth, invalid URI and no absolute ancestor.

four_deliberate_negatives.purpose: The chain is defective in exactly one way, and four sibling conditions are deliberately excluded so the diagnosis is unambiguous. Each was measured against the fixture rather than assumed; if any of the four stopped holding, the diagnosis recorded in this file would be wrong and the file would need re-deriving rather than the test re-running.

not_a_dangling_reference.assertion: every referenced identifier has an entry in originalUriBaseIds
not_a_dangling_reference.evidence: The referencing sites are exhaustive: results[0] and results[1] name %SRCROOT%, results[2] names SRCROOT, entry %SRCROOT% names %PROJECTROOT% and entry SRCROOT names PROJECTROOT. The map's keys are exactly %SRCROOT%, %PROJECTROOT%, SRCROOT and PROJECTROOT, so every one of those four references resolves to an entry and resolve_uri_base never takes its absent branch.

not_a_cycle.assertion: no identifier repeats along either walk
not_a_cycle.evidence: The %SRCROOT% walk visits %SRCROOT% then %PROJECTROOT%; the SRCROOT walk visits SRCROOT then PROJECTROOT. Both are two distinct identifiers, and the map's four keys are themselves distinct. The visited-identifier set in resolve_uri_base is therefore never triggered, and the outcome cannot be cycle.

not_over_depth.assertion: the chain is two nodes, well inside the bound
not_over_depth.evidence: len(chain) is 2 for both walks against paths.SARIF_BASE_CHAIN_MAX_DEPTH of 8. The depth check is evaluated on every iteration and never becomes true, so the outcome cannot be over-depth.
not_over_depth.depth_bound_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, SARIF_BASE_CHAIN_MAX_DEPTH = 8, the max_depth default of resolve_uri_base

not_an_invalid_uri.assertion: every URI in the document parses as a URI reference
not_an_invalid_uri.evidence: Classified every string in the document whose JSON pointer ends in /uri -- seven of them -- with paths.parse_uri_reference. Four are the base entries: 'spark-src/' relative, 'file:///opt/' file-uri, 'src/' relative, 'project/' relative. Three are the results' artifactLocation uris, all relative. None is URI_FORM_INVALID, so the outcome cannot be invalid-uri and the rejection class cannot be invalid_uri.
not_an_invalid_uri.entries_are_objects: All four originalUriBaseIds entries are JSON objects and all four uris are strings, so the entry-is-not-an-artifactLocation-object and uri-is-not-a-string sub-routes to BASE_OUTCOME_INVALID_URI are equally not in play.
not_an_invalid_uri.no_single_leading_slash: The set of /uri strings beginning with exactly one slash is empty, checked document-wide, so the SARIF errata issue 480 reading is not exercised here either.
not_an_invalid_uri.no_dot_dot_segments: The set of /uri strings carrying a .. segment is empty, so nothing here tests the errata's prohibition on normalizing .. out of a path.
not_an_invalid_uri.no_archive_marker: No /uri string carries an '!' , so no archive-member serialization is exercised.

four_deliberate_negatives.sole_fault: The outermost base of the second chain, PROJECTROOT, is relative. That single property is the whole defect, and it is what the rejection is attributable to.

distinguished_from.reject-sarif-uribaseid-missing-base.sari: That fixture's defective record names %REPOSITORYROOT%, which has no entry in the map: the walk stops on the first iteration with outcome 'absent' and a chain of one, and because 'absent' is fallback-eligible that record resolves to a row under the metadata this provisioning ships and rejects only where no explicit base is recorded. Here every identifier is present, the chain completes, and the outcome is not fallback-eligible -- so this fixture has one outcome where that one has two.
distinguished_from.reject-sarif-uribaseid-cycle.sarif: There the chain BASE_A -> BASE_B -> BASE_C returns to BASE_A and the visited set fires; the assertion that fixture exists for is that the walk terminates at all. Termination is never in question here: this walk has a natural end, and what it lacks at that end is an absolute value. Outcome 'cycle', fallback-eligible, against 'no-absolute-ancestor', not.
distinguished_from.reject-sarif-uribaseid-overdepth.sarif: There forty distinct identifiers chain to an absolute file:///opt/spark-src/ and only the depth bound stops the walk, at eight, with the remaining entries never read. Here the chain is two and the bound is never approached. Both guards -- the visited set and the depth bound -- are quiet in this fixture, which is precisely what leaves the absoluteness check as the only thing that can fail.
distinguished_from.reject-sarif-uribaseid-invalid-uri.sarif: There an entry's own uri is 'file://[not-a-valid-host/', which will not parse, so the walk returns 'invalid-uri' and the record is rejected under the class invalid_uri rather than unresolvable_path. That is a different class, not merely a different detail. Every uri here parses.
distinguished_from.reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.sarif: That fixture's defective record shares this one's class, unresolvable_path, and nothing else: its uri is 'urn:example:no-such-coordinate', a foreign scheme classified before any base is consulted, so its walk never runs. Sharing a class is exactly why the detail is quoted in both files -- the class alone cannot tell a chain with no absolute ancestor from a coordinate that names nothing in the tree.
distinguished_from.the_degenerate_base_case: A base that resolves to the filesystem root -- file:/// for a git-repository target, trivy issue 10364 -- returns outcome 'degenerate' and is fallback-eligible. It is not one of the five fixtures and is not this one: PROJECTROOT does not resolve to '/' , it does not resolve at all.

conditionality.what_is_unconditional: Everything this file states. The walk's termination, its outcome, the rejection, its class, its detail, the two surviving rows and every count are the same under any runner metadata. That is the property that separates this fixture from its dangling-base sibling, and it is why this file carries one canonical outcome at the top level rather than a branch table inside rows, rejections, counts and counters.
conditionality.authority: AAP 0.5.4 states the three terminal cases and routes only the first through the documented degenerate-base fallback: "a base identifier absent from originalUriBaseIds, or a chain that cycles or exceeds the depth, resolves through the runner-recorded base only where the runner metadata supplies an explicit base for that tool, and is otherwise a rejection under unresolvable_path; an entry whose URI is syntactically invalid is a rejection; and a chain that terminates on a relative reference with no absolute ancestor is a rejection."
conditionality.implementation_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py implements exactly that. BASE_OUTCOME_NO_ABSOLUTE_ANCESTOR is deliberately absent from paths.BASE_OUTCOMES_ELIGIBLE_FOR_METADATA_FALLBACK, whose four members are absent, cycle, over-depth and degenerate; and resolve_sarif_location tests `if not walk.eligible_for_metadata_fallback:` BEFORE it tests `if not tool_base.has_explicit_base:`, returning the rejection with the walk's own detail. The module's comment at that branch names the case: "BASE_OUTCOME_NO_ABSOLUTE_ANCESTOR: case 3, which AAP 0.5.4 rejects outright rather than routing through the metadata fallback."
conditionality.the_gate_order_is_the_assertion: Eligibility is checked first and the metadata second, so the metadata cannot rescue this record. A test that only asserted the class would pass against an implementation that had the two gates the other way round, because that implementation would also reject -- but only where no explicit base was recorded, and this provisioning records one. The control under branches[0].precondition.control is what separates the two implementations.
conditionality.the_rejection_detail_proves_the_gate_ord: The expected detail is the walk's detail verbatim, with no metadata clause appended. The fallback-eligible route appends "; and the runner metadata records path_base.kind ... with no explicit base for 'opengrep', so the documented degenerate-base fallback does not apply ..." to its detail; the absence of that clause here is observable evidence that the metadata was never consulted for this record.
conditionality.divergence_recorded: The agent prompt for this file describes the outcome as conditional on the runner metadata supplying an explicit path_base -- a row and parse status clean where one exists, a counted rejection and parse status partial where none does -- as with the dangling-base sibling. Measured against paths.py and AAP 0.5.4 that is not so for this condition: absent, cycle and over-depth are the fallback-eligible outcomes and are therefore metadata-conditional, while no-absolute-ancestor and invalid-uri are rejected outright and are unconditional. Recorded rather than quietly resolved, and recorded rather than followed: writing a Branch A row here would contradict the AAP, contradict the module, and put an expectation in this folder that the adapter cannot satisfy. The sibling expected/reject-sarif-uribaseid-cycle.rows.json records the same distinction from the other side, independently. What survives of the prompt's point, and what this file honours in full, is that both metadata states must be recorded with their own rows, rejections and arithmetic -- which is what /branches does, and the finding is that they coincide.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below -- the canonical two and their copies under each branch -- carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

expectation_form: unconditional-single-outcome, recorded across both metadata branches

expectation_form_note.canonical_expectation: /rows, /row_derivations, /rejections, /counts and /counters. This file is a single-outcome expected file in the shape of expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json, so the generic loader written for the cycle, over-depth and invalid-uri siblings reads it unchanged.
expectation_form_note.branches_are_a_view_not_a_second_measure: /branches carries the two metadata states the agent prompt requires recorded, each with its own precondition, rows, rejection and arithmetic. Their rows and rejections are required deep-equal to the canonical ones -- the invariants under cross_branch_invariants say so, and a test asserts it -- so the repetition is checked rather than trusted. A number that can drift inside one document is a number that will, which is why the counters are stated once, at /counters, and each branch points at them.
expectation_form_note.why_both_are_carried: A reader coming from the dangling-base sibling expects /branches and would read a missing key as an unanswered question; a loader coming from the other three siblings expects the top level. Carrying both, with the equality asserted, answers each without leaving the other to infer anything.

root_precondition.why: The surviving rows require this root. The resolving chain names it absolutely -- %PROJECTROOT% is file:///opt/ and %SRCROOT% is spark-src/ beneath it -- so both records resolve to /opt/spark-src/<uri> whatever root the adapter is given. Relativized against this root each returns its uri unchanged, is path_kind tree_file and takes in_scope true; relativized against any other root each would acquire a ../ prefix, become outside_root and take in_scope false, and the expected rows below would legitimately not match. No absolute path appears anywhere in this file regardless.
root_precondition.source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, spark_src -- read as input through paths.metadata_scan_root, never assumed
root_precondition.rejection_is_root_independent: The rejection is not root-dependent at all. resolve_uri_base never sees the root, and the walk fails before any relativization is attempted, so the class, the detail and the count are identical under any absolute root. That asymmetry is worth stating: a test that changed the root would change the rows and leave the rejection untouched.
root_precondition.consequence_for_the_test: A test exercising this fixture passes the recorded scan root, in both branches, with or without a trailing slash.

resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the opengrep entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.path_basis_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, BASIS_SARIF_BASE_CHAIN. Both surviving rows carry it because their chain completed on its own evidence. Neither carries BASIS_SARIF_METADATA_BASE (sarif-degenerate-base-metadata-fallback), which is the basis of a record rescued by the runner-recorded base -- the value expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json records, because that fixture's run emits no originalUriBaseIds at all. The two are different bases and neither value may be copied from the other file.

walk_outcomes_per_base.%PROJECTROOT%: the absolute ancestor of that chain, file:///opt/ , beneath which the accumulated level spark-src/ is joined
walk_outcomes_per_base.SRCROOT: no-absolute-ancestor -- chain SRCROOT -> PROJECTROOT, no base
walk_outcomes_per_base.PROJECTROOT: the terminal entry of that chain: uri 'project/' , relative, carrying no uriBaseId of its own

resolution_context.walk_outcome_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, resolve_uri_base and the BASE_OUTCOME_* constants. The outcome for %SRCROOT% is BASE_OUTCOME_RESOLVED with detail "resolved through %SRCROOT% -> %PROJECTROOT% to '/opt/spark-src'"; the outcome for SRCROOT is BASE_OUTCOME_NO_ABSOLUTE_ANCESTOR with the detail quoted under terminal_case.walk_detail.
resolution_context.the_two_chains_are_the_fixture: One map carries a conformant chain and a defective one, differing only in whether the outermost entry is absolute. That is what makes the fixture a test of the absoluteness check rather than of chaining: two records resolve through the legal chain and one terminates on the relative one, so the guard is shown to reject the defect without disabling the chaining SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.14.14 requires. A fixture whose every chain was defective could not show that.
resolution_context.chaining_is_legal: An originalUriBaseIds entry may itself carry a uriBaseId, and the specification's own section 3.14.14 example does exactly that, expressing SRCROOT relative to PROJECTROOT. A consumer that read one level would be wrong on conformant input: it would take the relative 'spark-src/' as the base and leave every path one directory short. The walk must follow the chain, and following a chain is what makes an unanchored end possible.
resolution_context.two_records_are_metadata_independent: The %SRCROOT% records never consult the runner metadata: resolve_sarif_location returns their path from the resolved chain before any fallback is considered. So the two rows would be identical in both branches even if the branch condition were live for this fixture -- which is a second, weaker reason the branches coincide, and not the reason. The reason is the eligibility gate, and it applies to the third record.
resolution_context.the_fault_is_the_base_map_not_the_uri: The defective record's uri, common/network-common/src/main/java/org/apache/spark/network/buffer/FileSegmentManagedBuffer.java, is a plain root-relative reference naming a real 155-line file in the pinned tree whose lines 112 to 114 are the record's own snippet verbatim. Pointed at %SRCROOT% -- one field, the derivation this fixture makes -- the identical record resolves to that path and is emitted, which is exactly what the positive sibling expected/opengrep.rows.json records as its row 0. Nothing about the path is wrong, and a reader who attributes the failure to the URI will look for the defect in the wrong place.
resolution_context.severity_source: No result in this fixture states a level of its own, and no rule carries properties.severity or properties.problem.severity, so each severity_native is the level its own rule states under defaultConfiguration.level -- SARIF 2.1.0's own derivation for a result that omits the property -- and each severity_norm comes from the SARIF level table: error High, warning Medium, note Low, none Info.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A SARIF result names a code location rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry.

rejection_boundary.statement: A chain that ends on a relative reference with no absolute ancestor is an unresolvable_path rejection, and it is a rejection under every runner metadata. Three of the five uriBaseId conditions resolve to a row where the metadata supplies an explicit base; this one and the invalid-URI one cannot, and this one shares its class with the three while sharing their conditionality with none of them.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: path is one of only two never-absent fields in the twelve-field schema, the other being severity_norm: emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS carries path, and emit.OPTIONAL_FIELDS is exactly severity_native, start_line, cwe, cve and package_coordinate. The defective record's own uri is relative, so it means nothing without a base, and the base it names cannot be established because the chain it heads never reaches an absolute value. There is therefore no path to put in the row, and counting the record under a named class is the only outcome that neither drops it nor invents a coordinate for it.

what_the_alternatives_would_have_produce.joining_the_relative_levels_together: A base of 'project/src' , which would relativize to a path with no relation to the scanned tree and a silent in_scope false. Plausible, unfalsifiable from the artifact, and wrong.
what_the_alternatives_would_have_produce.falling_back_to_the_runner_recorded_base: A row whose path is correct by accident: the record's uri happens to be root-relative, so joining it onto /opt/spark-src would produce the same path the positive sibling emits for the unmodified record. That is precisely why this must not happen -- an implementation that inverted the two gates would pass a test that only compared paths, and would then apply the same guess to a record whose uri was genuinely relative to something else.
what_the_alternatives_would_have_produce.dropping_the_record: The reconciliation identity would fail, 3 != 2 + 0, which is the arithmetic's purpose.

diagnosis_is_the_absoluteness_check_alon.the_identifier_resolves: The result names SRCROOT and the map carries an entry for it, so the absent branch is never taken. Not the missing-base case.
diagnosis_is_the_absoluteness_check_alon.the_chain_is_well_formed: Two links, SRCROOT -> PROJECTROOT, no identifier revisited and depth 2 against a bound of 8. Neither the cycle case nor the over-depth case.
diagnosis_is_the_absoluteness_check_alon.every_uri_parses: All seven /uri strings in the document are valid URI references and every entry is an object with a string uri, so none of the five sub-routes to BASE_OUTCOME_INVALID_URI is taken. Not the invalid-URI case.
diagnosis_is_the_absoluteness_check_alon.no_scheme_and_no_slash: The defective record's own uri is an ordinary relative reference: no scheme, so the foreign-scheme rejection that precedes base resolution is not taken; no leading slash, so the errata-480 reading is not taken; no '!' , so the archive route is not taken.
diagnosis_is_the_absoluteness_check_alon.what_is_left: Only whether the chain reached an absolute value. It did not, and that is the whole of the rejection.
diagnosis_is_the_absoluteness_check_alon.the_near_miss_that_proves_the_boundary: Give PROJECTROOT the uri 'file:///opt/' -- or give it a uriBaseId naming an entry that has one -- and the same chain resolves, the same record is emitted, and the fixture stops testing anything. That is the one-character neighbourhood the check occupies, and it is why the four negatives above are recorded as measurements rather than as remarks.

rejection_boundary.kept_separate_because: AAP 0.5.4 names the terminal cases rather than collapsing them. Four of the five reach the same rejection class, so the class alone cannot say which happened -- the sub-reason in the rejection detail is what distinguishes them, and a single merged fixture would lose the ability to diagnose why a path failed to resolve.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of runs[].results[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction
counts.raw_count_authority: normalize.reconcile.count_records("opengrep", doc), whose SARIF traversal sums the length of each run's results array and builds no row, resolves no path and maps no severity. It is the independent half of the identity: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows would satisfy the assertion while testing nothing. It reads no originalUriBaseIds and walks no chain, so this fixture's defect cannot reach it -- which is what keeps the left-hand side fixed at 3 whatever the walk does, and identical in both branches.
counts.raw_excludes_the_two_notifications: The run's two toolExecutionNotifications and its four originalUriBaseIds entries are not results and are counted by neither the adapter nor count_records. Counting either would move this figure and break the identity.
counts.rejections_by_class_note: One class, one record. The other nine members of paths.REJECT_CLASSES are absent from this fixture, and a per-class reading that reported them as zero rather than as absent would be equally correct here; what matters is that the single entry names unresolvable_path exactly.
counts.identity_holds_in_both_branches: Same left side, same right side. The branches are recorded because the prompt requires both metadata states answered, not because the arithmetic differs between them.

four_reported_counters.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- the four counts reported per tool
four_reported_counters.note: Named here rather than restated with their values. The counters block below is the single measurement, and a number carried twice inside one document is a number that can drift; counters_note gives the reason each of the four is zero.

counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = "partial", assigned as partial where there are rejections and clean where there are none. Partial is right precisely because the adapter did not abandon the artifact: every parsable record was emitted and the one rejected record is counted under its class, with its reason retained. This is deliberately not normalize.reconcile's STATUS_PASS / STATUS_FAIL / STATUS_NOT_APPLICABLE vocabulary, which describes an assertion's outcome rather than an artifact's parse.
counts.parse_status_is_partial_in_both_branches: The agent prompt expects clean in the explicit-base branch. It is partial there too, because the record is rejected there too; conditionality.divergence_recorded states why, and no branch of this file records clean.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): twenty authored keys, one path_kind_* per paths.PATH_KINDS and one severity_basis_* per severity.BASIS_VALUES, twenty-nine in total. All twenty-nine are stated above, so a zero is visibly measured rather than missing. They are identical in both branches and are therefore measured once here; each branch points at this block rather than repeating it.
counters_note: Four things a reader must not "correct". First, rule_id_from_rule_id is 3 while the severity, path-kind and scope counters are 2: the rule step is step 2 of the adapter's classification order and the path step is step 4, so the rejected record resolves its rule identifier before it is rejected and never reaches severity, never yields a path kind and never has its scope evaluated. That asymmetry is the classification order made visible, not a miscount. Second, start_line_absent is 0 rather than 1: step 5 is never reached for the rejected record, so its region.startLine of 112 is neither examined nor counted as absent -- and non_integer_start_line is not in play either, which is worth saying because the defective record does carry a perfectly valid startLine. Third, severity_from_rule_default_configuration is 2 rather than severity_from_level: no result in this fixture states a level of its own, so each row's level is the one its rule states. Fourth, all four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool are 0: every result carries exactly one location, so multi_location_records is 0 -- and it is counted before the path step, so it would have been 0 even had the defective record carried several; the rule that names a weakness names exactly one, so multi_valued_cwe_records is 0; no rule string carries a CVE identifier, so multi_valued_cve_records is 0; and both emitted paths name a file inside the scanned tree, so non_filesystem_paths is 0.

rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_UNRESOLVABLE_PATH constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, the closed set of ten. Written verbatim rather than paraphrased, and asserted against the module rather than by eye: a test that only counts rejections cannot tell one condition from another, so the class name is what carries the assertion.
rejections.reject_class_covers_the_sub_reason_in_de: AAP 0.5.4 names one class for the whole family of base failures and puts which case it was in the detail. paths.REJECT_CLASS_DESCRIPTIONS says so in the module: the class covers "no establishable base, a uriBaseId that is absent, cyclic, over-depth or degenerate with no explicit runner-recorded base, a chain with no absolute ancestor, or a bytecode class no source file in the tree declares". So this class alone does not distinguish this fixture from the dangling-base, cycle, over-depth and unresolvable-path siblings, and a test that asserts only the class is asserting less than the fixture establishes.
rejections.classification_step: step 4 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. Steps 1 to 3 all pass on this record: it is a JSON object, it carries a valid ruleId that resolves to /runs/0/tool/driver/rules/0, and it carries a non-empty message.text. That is deliberate, so the only thing left to reject it for is its path.
rejections.start_line_never_examined: Step 5 is never reached, so this record's region.startLine of 112 is never examined and non_integer_start_line is not in play. Worth stating because the fixture does give the defective record a valid startLine -- the positive sibling emits exactly that value for the unmodified record -- so a reader could otherwise expect an interaction between the two conditions.
rejections.severity_never_resolved: The severity step follows the path step, so the rejected record's rule level never reaches severity.py and never reaches the LiteralTally. Its rule's 'error' literal appears in severity-map.md only through row 1, which cites the same rule -- that document reports literals against the rows the dataset contains.
rejections.scope_never_evaluated: in_scope is computed from a resolved path, so it is never computed here. The record's uri would have matched the glob common/network-common/src/main/** had it resolved -- stating that is not a claim about the row it does not produce, and rows_out_of_scope stays 0 rather than absorbing it.
rejections.uri_note: The uri is a plain root-relative reference naming a real 155-line file in the pinned tree, and the positive sibling resolves the identical record to exactly that path under the unmodified base. Nothing about it is malformed, out of scope or foreign-schemed; it carries no leading slash, no .. segment and no archive marker. The rejection is caused entirely by the chain the identifier heads having no absolute ancestor.
rejections.uri_base_id_walk_detail: the chain SRCROOT -> PROJECTROOT ends on the relative reference 'project/' with no uriBaseId to resolve it against, so no absolute ancestor exists
rejections.eligibility_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, BASE_OUTCOMES_ELIGIBLE_FOR_METADATA_FALLBACK -- absent, cycle, over-depth and degenerate. BASE_OUTCOME_NO_ABSOLUTE_ANCESTOR is deliberately not a member, and BaseResolution.eligible_for_metadata_fallback is therefore false for this walk.
rejections.fallback_refused_because: The outcome is not eligible, so resolve_sarif_location returns the rejection at the eligibility gate and never reaches the has_explicit_base gate. This is the whole difference from the dangling-base sibling, where the outcome is eligible and the metadata then decides.
rejections.expected_detail: the chain SRCROOT -> PROJECTROOT ends on the relative reference 'project/' with no uriBaseId to resolve it against, so no absolute ancestor exists
rejections.expected_detail_note: The walk's detail verbatim, with nothing appended. A fallback-eligible outcome refused for want of an explicit base carries a second clause naming path_base.kind; its absence here is observable evidence that the metadata was never consulted, and it is identical in both branches for that reason. A test may assert this detail by full-string equality, unlike its dangling-base sibling's, because no part of it depends on the metadata.
rejections.record_identity_note: The adapter supplies run_index, result_index and rule_id; the resolver adds the raw uri and, where one is present as a non-empty string, the raw uriBaseId -- in that order, which is the order recorded above. Enough to find the record in the artifact again, and never the record itself and never a secret value.
rejections.why_not_a_row: There is no path to put in the row. path is never absent from a row, so a record whose coordinate cannot be expressed against the scan root has no valid row representation, and the alternatives -- dropping it, or joining it onto a base nothing anchored -- would each hide it. Counting it under a named class keeps it visible and keeps the arithmetic honest.
rejections.root_independent: The class, the detail and the count are the same under any absolute scan root: the walk fails before the root is used for anything.

prohibitions_observed.no_apache_spark_file_touched: The pinned tree was read only -- three files, for their line counts and their snippet text. No source file, pom, workflow or .gitignore was modified, and no runner, harness helper or allowlist was edited.
